feeds.title: Mirrix Tapestry & Bead Looms Blog
feeds.description: Mirrix Looms are bead and tapestry looms for everyone from the novice crafter to the professional artist. We don't just make looms, we weave on them too. We ensure that every piece of equipment we design and manufacture is engineered to accomplish its single task: to allow its user to easily create a professional-quality piece of artwork.

feeds.title: Schacht Spindle
feeds.description: Here at Schacht Spindle Company we are deeply committed to excellence in our work, and above all, to your satisfaction. Today, we build our looms in a 35,000 square foot factory with 25 employees, and are one of the world's leading makers of handweaving looms and spinning wheels. We have been designing handweaving and handspinning equipment since 1969.

feeds.title: The Weave Shed
feeds.description: The Weave Shed is a website for weave designers with a portfolio practice, payee, mills, independent, designer makers, tapestry, artists, educators and students. The site was initially funded for the for the first two years by The Worshipful Company of Weavers and Central Saint Martins, University of The Arts London.

feeds.title: Backstrap Weaving
feeds.description: My weaving , my indigenous teachers, my inspiration, tutorials and more.

feeds.title: Tien Chiu
feeds.description: I'm a weaver who is fascinated by the potential of cloth. I began my weaving career with handwoven garments, such as my Kodachrome Jacket (featured on the cover of Handwoven Magazine), and my handwoven, couture-sewn wedding dress (now part of the permanent collection at the American Textile History Museum).

feeds.title: Vritti Designs
feeds.description: Vritti is a merge of traditional illumination where ethnicity meets modern trend. The word 'Vritti', originates from Sanskrit language, which means a serene wave emerging from mind which eliminates the evil mental disturbance and allows you to indulge into eternal peace.

feeds.title: Matt Tommey Blog
feeds.description: Matt Tommey makes North Carolina baskets for modern rustic decor out of natural materials straight from the mountains of Asheville.

feeds.title: ASpinnerWeaver
feeds.description: For over 35 years I have been weaving on an inkle loom. This type of loom makes narrow pieces, no more than 6' in width. Within this narrow constraint, there are endless possibilities for combining colors into patterns. When I create a woven piece, I want it to be both functional and beautiful. I have created many types of useful everyday items including: shoelaces, scarves, belts, bags & clothing

feeds.title: Flora & Fiber Blog
feeds.description: This is the Flora & Fiber blog containing posts about fiber arts, events, products, and related interests. Debby Greenlaw is the owner of Flora & Fiber, an artisan fiber arts studio that offers a simple, fun approach to preserving and creating handcrafted traditions.

feeds.title: Peggy Osterkamp's Weaving Blog
feeds.description: Peggy Osterkamp's special skill is making the richness of her training and experience accessible to students. In the series, Peggy Osterkamp's New Guide to Weaving, she presents a wealth of weaving knowledge and research, much of it never available before in the United States.

feeds.title: Tapestry 13
feeds.description: I am Tommye McClure Scanlin, an artist who observes and responds to my surroundings for inspiration. My primary artistic medium is handwoven tapestry, an ancient method of working with fibers to create images.

feeds.title: Random Acts of Color
feeds.description: I live in Rochester, NY, where there's lots of water -- Lake Ontario, the Genesee River, and the wonderful Finger Lakes -- and lots of winter! Weaving and the fiber arts sustain me through all the seasons.

feeds.title: Tottie Talks Crafts Blog
feeds.description: I am an artist, designer. I am passionate about the fiber arts: I love love love small loom weaving, crochet, knitting, spool knitting, tatting, doll making, spinning, and woodworking that relates to the fiber arts.

feeds.title: Plain Weave and beyond
feeds.description: I am a hand-weaver. I believe that cloth and its creation are somehow embedded in our DNA. Making cloth seems fundamental to me; I am saddened by the distance we have created between the fabric that means so much to us (wedding dresses, christening gowns, tallitot, baby blankets and grandma's quilt) and the making of that fabric.

feeds.title: Weaving a Life
feeds.description: In 1975 I was looking for a career that would fascinate me for the rest of my life. In a way, weaving chose me! In this blog you will find posts for weaving.

feeds.title: Buellwood Weaver and Fiber Guild
feeds.description: A blog about weaving.

feeds.title: Durham Weaver
feeds.description: I am a designer weaver and love to use natural yarns in my work, such as linen, silk, alpaca, cashmere and merino wool. I am fascinated by the long history of weaving and research ancient textiles and the techniques used to produce them.

feeds.title: ArgoKnot
feeds.description: ArgoKnot is a journal of the author's weaving, spinning, and knitting life. Check out the posts the sections like Basketry, Bobbin Lace, Gallery of Baskets, Gallery of Loom Woven Pieces, spinning, Tapestry Gallery, weaving, and more. View the woven work and learn more about weaving.

feeds.title: Daryl's Blog
feeds.description: Between the sewing machine and the loom, my journey in the fiber arts has taken over 45 years. From an alterations business at 15, to production hand-woven clothing, to custom art to wear, my work has covered, adorned, and embellished the female body for as long as I can remember.

feeds.title: Susan Harvey
feeds.description: A journal about my weaving 'meanderings'. I have been weaving now for twenty years. I like finer threads and natural fibres such as silks and exotic blends, linen and cottons. I also love tencel and its bright colors.

feeds.title: 14 Mile Farm Blog
feeds.description: At 14 Mile Farm, Jasmine crafts artisanal textiles with deep intention, from hand-dyed yarns to handwoven luxury fabrics. As a weaver, healer, and mother living in an Alaskan cabin, she shares stories in fibre, wool, and cloth, offering wearable art and heirloom home goods imbued with love and magic.

feeds.title: Warped Fibers Blog
feeds.description: Weaving and Fiber Art blog by Nicole Bunting. A new blog post every Wednesday with weaving tips, tricks, puns, and info to get you started.

feeds.title: The Good Yarn Blog
feeds.description: The Good Yarn has Exceptional Customer service & everything for Spinning, Weaving, Felting, Dyeing & Carding supplies. On my blog, you can read, learn and find free patterns.

feeds.title: My Tapestry Journeys
feeds.description: Tapestry Journeys is a weekly blog about all things tapestry including educational and inspirational content by tapestry artist Kennita Tully.

feeds.title: Rebecca Mezoff Blog
feeds.description: Rebecca Mezoff writes about all things tapestry weaving including tapestry looms, weft and warp yarn, tapestry weaving techniques, and lots of free weaving tips. The author of The Art of Tapestry Weaving loves to share her adventures in tapestry on the blog.

feeds.title: Cally Booker Blog
feeds.description: Cally Booker is a handweaver, textile designer, writer, and teacher. Weaving is a craft that can be meticulously planned or improvised at the loom, and a combination of these approaches appeals to the different parts of my nature. Cally Booker is passionate about making things by hand. Read her Cally Booker blog to know more about her work, her techniques, useful advice, trending designs, product reviews, and material description.

feeds.title: Crazy as a Loom
feeds.description: I am an 'older' woman, who refuses to get old. I think I am really twelve, and my family will often agree. I have found my passion in weaving, and have left one career to begin another.

feeds.title: Ullvuna
feeds.description: By Florencia Campos Correa, DIY craft project, weaving loom instructions, how to weave, pin loom weaving, crochet, needlecrafts, do it yourself, craft book, Ullvuna patterns designs, and video lessons. Crochet and weaving projects, tips, freebies, and more.

feeds.title: Tuesday Weavers
feeds.description: We are the Tuesday Weavers, a lively group of weavers from all levels and all walks of life. We meet every Tuesday at the Appalachian Arts Craft Center in Norris, Tennessee for weaving, learning, fellowship and a lot of laughter.

feeds.title: K Spoering
feeds.description: K Spoering is a Contemporary tapestry designer and weaver, oil painter.

feeds.title: Mississauga Handweavers and Spinners Guild
feeds.description: This blog Provides information on meetings and program for a weaving spinning guild.

feeds.title: Dianne's Loom Talk | My Adventures in Hand Weaving
feeds.description: Dianne is passionate about fibre and weaving. She weaves exquisite fine wraps, scarves and fabric and scrumptious mohair blankets from natural fibres.

feeds.title: Reno Fiber Guild
feeds.description: A blog about the Reno Fiber Guild - weavers and spinners organization in northern Nevada.

feeds.title: Thrums
feeds.description: A journal about weaving meanderings by Susan Harvey. She has been weaving now for twenty-four years. Spinning, Dyeing, Crochet, Reading, and Music are some of her other interests.

feeds.title: The Weaving Loom | The Modern Weaver's Resource
feeds.description: Hi I'm Kate. I've created this blog to share my love of weaving and help creatives like you learn how to weave too. Here you will find posts for how to weave, how to do different techniques and much more.

feeds.title: Free Bead Patterns and Ideas
feeds.description: A blog about bead weaving patterns. Find new ideas to make wonderful handmade jewelry like necklaces, bracelets, christmas ornaments and more.

feeds.title: Elizabeth Buckley Tapestry Artist Blog
feeds.description: Elizabeth Buckley writes her observations and experiences of life as an artist. She is a second-generation tapestry artist of over fifty years. Elizabeth first wove tapestry based on the Mexican and Rio Grande techniques and then expanded into those of Peter Collingwood's rug weaving.

feeds.title: The Weaving Song
feeds.description: A Weaving Blog by Michiele.

feeds.title: Dust Bunnies Under My Loom
feeds.description: Hi, I am Lynnette. My goal is to get my 'bum on the weaving bench' as often as possible. I love to see huge dust bunnies growing under my loom as the fibres fall from my reed, a sure sign that I'm actively weaving! My primary focus is to create beautiful and unique fashion accessories and table linens for sale.

feeds.title: House Weaving
feeds.description: Part architectural designer, part fiber artist. Living in Portland, Oregon, I've learned what it's like to chase landscapes and immerse myself in the beauty of the Pacific Northwest. I think of my loom as a way to translate the terrain into fiber design and explore this woven lifestyle.

feeds.title: Warp & Weave | Articles on color in weaving
feeds.description: Learn about color in handweaving. Pick colors that stay bright when woven, make your pattern show, use painted warps, understand color mixing, and much more!

feeds.title: Warped for Good
feeds.description: Hi, I am Karen Isenhower. Handweaving is a field rich with these treasures, and I enjoy sharing what I find. I'll let you know right up front that I'm still learning, that I don't always know what I'm talking about, and that I do make mistakes. Here you will find weaving patterns for your own projeects.

feeds.title: American Tapestry Alliance
feeds.description: The American Tapestry Alliance (ATA) is a non-profit organization supporting the fine arts medium of contemporary handwoven tapestry

feeds.title: Loom & Spindle Blog
feeds.description: Hi, my name is Andrea. I'm a self taught passionate free-form weaver, hand spinner and creative thinker based in Melbourne's south east. In Loom & Spindle blog you'll find a range of weaving and spinning tutorials that will help and inspire your own projects.

feeds.title: Curious Weaver
feeds.description: Curiousweaver studio is woven together by Kaz (Karen) Madigan. A weaver for almost 40 years, since 2011 she has been specialising in Saori weaving and is the first registered Saori studio in Australia. 'As a weaver for many years I have explored and tried many types of weaving. I love it all. I've walked in shoes of the artist, craftsman, designer, maker, author, teacher and artisan.

feeds.title: Weft Blown | Handwoven textiles, Looms & Spinning Wheels
feeds.description: I am a textile designer and I create unique weather inspired handwoven items for you and your home. I also teach weaving, spinning, and other yarn related crafts at my studio in West Kilbride.

feeds.title: The Loom Room
feeds.description: Stacey Harvey-Brown has been teaching weaving since 2005, firstly at The Loom Room in the UK and now, from her new studio near Nérac, in the heart of Gascony, SW France.

feeds.title: Meg Weaves
feeds.description: My name is Meg Nakagawa. I am a handweaver in Nelson, New Zealand. I grew up watching my mother knit, sew, and embroider while listening to her chant how she yearned to weave. That weaving is the ultimate textile work thus became my creed. Mom started weaving when she was 60.

feeds.title: Pinkmaharani | Finest Handwoven Cashmere Shawls
feeds.description: Pink maharani was started with the values that we create something where we place people, animals and the planet always first. We do this by not compromising on neither quality nor aesthetics. We strive to make the finest handwoven cashmere, which is both beautiful and impactful.

feeds.title: Dani Ortman | Handwoven
feeds.description: Handwoven Scarves & Textiles, Weaving a journey to remember. Designed and hand woven on a traditional floor loom by Canadian designer/handweaver Dani Ortman.

feeds.title: Wonder Woven LLC
feeds.description: Wonder Woven LLC is a weaving studio in Santa Monica, CA focused on crafting beautiful and comfortable wraps for wearing your baby or toddler. It is the creative endeavor of Tracy Desrosiers Bromwich, a liscensed architect and mother of 3.

feeds.title: AVL Looms
feeds.description: Global manufacturer of technologically advanced, finely crafted weaving equipment for the novice to the expert. AVL serves customers in the crafts, education, industrial sampling and production handweaving markets.

feeds.title: Etsy BeadWeavers
feeds.description: The Esty BeadWeavers is made up of bead artists who aspire to successfully market their beadwoven creations on Etsy.com and elsewhere. The Beadweavers' creations are different from many of the traditional beaded items, in that they are woven from hundreds or thousands of tiny beads to create intricate designs and pictures. These weavings take the form of both art and jewelry.

feeds.title: Helena Loermans Handwoven Textiles
feeds.description: My weaving studio is in the historic town of Odemira in Portugal. I am a passionate hand weaver.

feeds.title: Not 2 Square Weavers
feeds.description: A blog about handweaving group in Nevada County, CA.

feeds.title: Cariboo Handwoven
feeds.description: My weaving ranges from classic and earthy to funky and energetic. I use heathery Shetland wools, soft but sturdy cottons, and my own handspun wool and alpaca. From the spark of an idea through to the meticulous fringing or hemming, my handwoven items are designed, produced and presented with joy and delight.

feeds.title: My Gentle Threads. . .
feeds.description: Welcome to my sacred space! I am entering my fifth year with my blog and it has been an incredible journey for me. I love to share my creative adventures, poetic words and photographic moments about weaving.

feeds.title: Banner Mountain Textiles
feeds.description: Handweaving blog by Beryl Moody.

feeds.title: Kindred Threads
feeds.description: My love of color and texture has taken me on a journey from being a glass artist to the fiber arts world. For the last 10 years I have explored spinning, dyeing and weaving. With a side trip into owning a yarn shop for a few years, I am now back to creating fine handwovens, handspun and hand dyed yarns, in my log home studio in the beautiful hills of southwestern Wisconsin.

feeds.title: Deanna's Weaving
feeds.description: I am a weaver. This blog will chronicle my experiences in weaving and other fiber crafts I enjoy.

feeds.title: Weaving in the Foothills
feeds.description: I enjoy almost all aspects of the art and craft of weaving yarn into cloth, looking at both color and structure as they influence the final product.

feeds.title: Qualicum Weavers and Spinners Guild
feeds.description: The Qualicum Weavers and Spinners Guild supports personal growth in the fibre arts through study groups, workshops, mentoring and sharing of experience.

feeds.title: Eweniquely ewe
feeds.description: A weaving blog by Cindie. In this blog you will find ideas and new inspiration for weaving.

feeds.title: Jean Williams | Hand Weaver
feeds.description: My journey into weaving began by watching one grandmother crochet, another quilt, seeing the rag rugs woven by my parents on the old loom in the basement. Weaving satisfies a curiosity for me. Beautiful textiles intrigue me and make me wonder how they 'work', how the weaver gets the threads to do what they do. And how can I use that technique?

feeds.title: Rep Weaver
feeds.description: Rep Weaver blog about hand weaving and related crafts including tatting, sewing etc.

feeds.title: Warped Minds
feeds.description: I am a handweaver and teacher of traditional textiles crafts, such as weaving, spinning, felt making and crochet.

feeds.title: Weaving in and out
feeds.description: A Weaving blog.

feeds.title: Sosumi Weaving
feeds.description: We design and hand weave fashion items for the person and the home.

feeds.title: Kristie Foss Creations
feeds.description: Learn the art and creativity of bead weaving. Also find various tips and ideas to create unique handmade jewelry.

feeds.title: Molly Elkind : Talking Textiles
feeds.description: A blog about hand weaving, tapestry, and the place of craft and art in contemporary life.

feeds.title: Daisy Hill Weaving Studio
feeds.description: It has been a dream of mine to learn weaving, ever since I was a child. My opportunity came early in 2005, when my sister-in-law let me borrow her countermarche loom. I had a couple friends help me understand the loom and get me started. Those first couple projects were exciting for me.

feeds.title: Carson Sierra Spinners and Weavers
feeds.description: A resource for practicing and aspiring fiber artists in and near Carson City, Nevada since 1976.

feeds.title: Gangewifre Weaving
feeds.description: A weaving blog of the what, why and how of the work I have been doing. Here you will find artcils about weaving and weaving equipment.

feeds.title: Kerstin's extras
feeds.description: I am a professional weaver from the south of Sweden.

feeds.title: Dimensional Weaving | Martina Celerin 3D fiber art
feeds.description: I am a fiber artist. I create 3 dimensional weavings using reclaimed and recycled materials. I love to create tapestries that are stories of the world around me - people I've met, places I've been and things that make me smile.

feeds.title: Hand Weaver's Guild of Lincoln
feeds.description: The Hand Weavers Guild of Lincoln (HWGL) is a diverse group of beginning to advanced weavers and artists who share an interest in the art of handweaving, spinning, and other fiber arts. The Guild offers educational opportunities and the exchange of ideas.

feeds.title: Woven Thoughts
feeds.description: A weaving blog.

feeds.title: Sandra's Loom Blog
feeds.description: I am a professional weaver, specializing in complex weaves using fine threads. Most of my studio work consists of scarves, shawls, and wraps woven on a 48-inch, 24-shaft computer-assisted AVL dobby loom or wall art woven on a 48-inch, 1,440-heddle AVL jacquard loom.

feeds.title: Nigel's Weaving Blog
feeds.description: A Weaving blog by Nigel.

feeds.title: Kay Faulkner's Blog
feeds.description: In May 2009, I had started this blog to record my adventures while completing an artist residency at Sturt, Mittagong, on the Southern Highlands of New South Wales, Australia. The residency finished in September. I have had such enthusiastic response from what I wrote that I have decided to continue to record my adventures both in and away from the studio.

feeds.title: A Fiber Artisan's Weaving Path
feeds.description: Deanna Jill Deeds is a Weaver, dyer, spinner, worker of sprang and other fiber techniques!

feeds.title: Camp Runamuck
feeds.description: A Weaving blog.

feeds.title: Alice Schlein | Weaverly
feeds.description: I'm Alice Schlein, a weaver and book maker in South Carolina. Occasionally I write about Photoshop, Network Drafting, bread baking, and whatever else strikes my fancy.

feeds.title: Weave a Real Peace Blog
feeds.description: Weave a Real Peace (WARP) is a networking organization of weavers, academics, and interested supporters who value the importance of textiles to communities around the world.
